'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[2021 Kandahar bombing]]
***Three [[suicide bombing|suicide bombers]] [[list of 2021 Afghanistan attacks|attack]] a [[Shia Islam in Afghanistan|Shiite]] [[mosque]] in [[Kandahar]], [[Afghanistan]], killing 47 people and injuring 70 others. The explosions occur at the main door and inside the mosque. [[Taliban]] authorities later arrived and secured the mosque. [[Ministry of Interior Affairs (Afghanistan)|Taliban interior ministry]] spokesman Qari Saeed Khosti says that authorities are currently collecting evidence in order to determine responsibility for the bombing. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/15/explosion-hits-shia-mosque-in-afghanistans-kandahar (Al Jazeera)]
***[[Islamic State – Khorasan Province|ISIL-K]] claims responsibility for the attack, reporting that two attackers shot and killed security guards outside the mosque before blowing themselves up inside, where people were worshipping. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/islamic-state-claims-responsibility-mosque-attack-afghan-city-kandahar-statement-2021-10-15/ (Reuters)]
**[[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan]]
***[[United States Marine Corps]] [[Lieutenant colonel (United States)|lieutenant colonel]] [[Stuart Scheller]] is reprimanded by a military judge following his criticism of the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]]’s handling of the withdrawal from [[Afghanistan]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/marine-officer-receives-reprimand-afghanistan-criticism-80608893 (ABC News)]
*[[Murder of David Amess]]
**[[David Amess]], United Kingdom [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|MP]] for [[Southend West (UK Parliament constituency)|Southend West]], is [[Assassination|stabbed to death]] in [[Leigh-on-Sea]], [[Essex]], while meeting constituents at Belfairs [[Methodist]] Church. The suspect was arrested at the scene, and [[Essex Police|police]] are not looking for anyone else in connection with the incident. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-58930593 (BBC News)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-58935372 (BBC News)]
*[[Anglophone Crisis]]
**A [[Cameroon]]ian policeman is [[lynched]] by a mob after he killed a five-year-old girl at a [[security checkpoint|checkpoint]] in [[Buea]] [[Southwest Region (Cameroon)|Southwest Region]]. Protests involving hundreds of people occurred after the killing of the child. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/14/cameroon-urges-calm-after-policeman-kills-schoolgirl-in-anglophone-region (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Central African Republic Civil War]]
**[[List of heads of state of the Central African Republic|President]] [[Faustin-Archange Touadéra]] declares a unilateral [[ceasefire]] with the [[Coalition of Patriots for Change]] and the [[anti-balaka]] [[militia]] groups. [https://www.barrons.com/news/c-africa-president-decrees-unilateral-conflict-ceasefire-01634320207?tesla=y (AFP via ''Barron's'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Four [[Human migration|migrant]]s are found dead by the [[Spain|Spanish]] [[Maritime Safety and Rescue Society]] in the [[Mediterranean Sea]] off the coast of [[Cape Trafalgar]] in the [[Province of Cádiz]] after their boat sank. The [[Customs Surveillance Service|coast guard]] reports that 21 others from the boat are missing. [https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/international/1634301321-four-migrants-dead-21-missing-off-coast-of-spain (AFP via i24 News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei]]
****[[Brunei]] surpasses 10,000 cases of [[COVID-19]] after reporting a record 423 new cases in the past 24 hours. [https://thescoop.co/2021/10/15/brunei-passes-10000-covid-cases-milestone-after-breaking-daily-record/ (''The Scoop'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] is expected to reopen its borders to overseas travellers as it relaxes COVID-19-related restrictions amid a decrease in the number of new cases. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-58880429 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines]]
****The [[Inter-Agency Task Force for the Management of Emerging Infectious Diseases]] announces that the [[National Capital Region]] will be downgraded to Alert Level 3 beginning on October 16, which will allow cinemas and [[theme park]]s to reopen for the first time since March 2020. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/metro-manila-alert-level-3-october-16-31-2021 (''Rappler'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in South Korea]]
****[[President of South Korea|President]] [[Moon Jae-in]] and [[First Lady of South Korea|first lady]] [[Kim Jung-sook]] receive [[booster dose]]s of the COVID-19 vaccine. [https://m-en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20211015002751315 (Yonhap News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]]
****The [[Brussels-Capital Region]] expands the use of the COVID Safe Ticket to the [[hospitality]] industry, [[sports centre]]s, and indoor events with more than 50 people. [https://www.brusselstimes.com/brussels/189262/covid-safe-ticket-mandatory-in-brussels-from-tomorrow-but-no-fines-yet/ (''The Brussels Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]]'s Green Pass becomes mandatory for all workplaces, but there are fears of disruption among transport workers and at ports where [[COVID-19 vaccination in Italy|COVID-19 vaccination rate]]s are relatively low. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-58913865 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the fourth consecutive day of 999 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 221,313. The country also reports a record for the second consecutive day of 32,196 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 7.92 million. [https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/72904/ (Interfax)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
*****A COVID-19 [[Vaccination policy|vaccination mandate]] comes into effect in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], with all essential workers required to have at least one dose of a [[World Health Organization]]-approved [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] to continue working. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/oct/15/victoria-covid-update-vaccine-mandate-takes-effect-as-state-records-2170-cases (''The Guardian Australia'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Papua New Guinea]]
****The [[COVID-19]] crisis worsens in [[Papua New Guinea]], as the [[government of Papua New Guinea|government]] seeks international help in order to combat the increase in new cases and deaths. The government has admitted to a slow response to the crisis and also blames [[vaccine hesitancy]] as part of the problem. The [[World Health Organization]] has agreed to help the country. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/453627/png-desparately-needs-overseas-help-to-fight-covid-19 (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Yukon]]
****[[Yukon]] imposes a [[COVID-19 vaccine]] mandate for sports facilities, restaurants and other non-essential services. The mandate will take effect on November 30. [https://www.yukon-news.com/news/yukon-government-announces-mandatory-vaccination-rules/ (''Yukon News'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**During an online emergency meeting, the [[foreign minister]]s of the [[ASEAN]] agree to exclude [[Myanmar]]'s [[Tatmadaw|military junta]] chief [[Min Aung Hlaing]] from the upcoming [[ASEAN Summit]] to be held later this month. The country will instead be represented by non-political representative at the [[Summit (meeting)|summit]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2021/10/16/Myanmar-junta-chief-excluded-from-summit-ASEAN (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
*[[Paramount leader]] [[Xi Jinping]] of the [[China|People's Republic of China]] will not attend in person the [[2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference|Cop26 climate change conference]] in [[Glasgow]], as it's told to [[Untied Kingdom|UK]] [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]]. The announcement comes amid international pessimism that, now compounded by the absence of China, a global leader in pollution and [[greenhouse gas]] emissions, the event would not result in any substantiative change. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/chinas-xi-snub-cop26-uk-pm-johnson-told-times-2021-10-15/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Masten Wanjala]], the [[Kenyans|Kenyan]] suspected [[serial killer]] of 14 boys, who escaped from prison two days ago, is [[murder]]ed by lynching by a mob of villagers in [[Bungoma]]. Wanjala was hiding at his parents' home when he was identified by neighbours. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-58923592 (BBC News)]
